authoredWrongPaths.feedback: Adding every value is the MEAN's opening move. The range only touches the endpoints: max − min.
The middle is the MEDIAN's territory — a center, not a spread. Range measures the stretch between min and max.
129 is max PLUS min (71 + 58). Range measures the gap between them: 71 − 58 = 13.
71 is just the maximum. The range asks how far the max sits ABOVE the min: 71 − 58 = 13.
12 is 10 + 2 — the endpoints added instead of subtracted. Range = 10 − 2 = 8.
10 is the maximum alone. Range measures the stretch from the min: 10 − 2 = 8.
The count doesn't drive the range at all — sets of different sizes can share a range, and same-size sets can differ. It's the shared ENDPOINTS (2 and 10) doing it.
Tempting, since the first set bunches within 6 ± something — but range is defined off the full endpoints: 10 − 2 = 8 for both. Measuring the bunched middle needs a better tool (next lesson).
9 was the OLD range (12 − 3). The 20-lap day is the new maximum, so the range stretches: 20 − 3 = 17.
8 is the jump from the old max to the new one (20 − 12). The range itself runs from the MIN: 20 − 3 = 17.
